responsibility: Machine-readable ownership and shrinking legacy-debt limits for the browser conversation surface.
invariants: Conversation Sync v3 snapshots and ordered events are the only inputs that mutate durable browser turn state.
TurnStore is the only normalized browser conversation state authority.
ConversationSurface is the only content-derived writer of the conversation DOM.
ConversationSurface owns the bounded DOM window, scroll anchor, and follow suspension without truncating TurnStore.
turnId is the only durable rendered identity and blockId is the only identity below a turn.
Conversation shells contain catalog and settings metadata only; settings persistence never depends on Turn presence.
Durable document state, live session state, and local interaction state never share an owner.

Translation display is a pure typed projection of authoritative Turn content plus turn-keyed local interaction state; browser task recovery only resumes lifecycle-local task IDs and never scans a parallel message model.
Diagnostics observe ConversationTurnRead and the active Surface without fetching or parsing another transcript.
HTML escaping and trusted-template branding have one typed owner; typed features import it directly instead of discovering policy through a mutable runtime registry.
Error normalization and error presentation have distinct typed owners; presentation receives translation and icon capabilities only at the composition boundary.
Turn provenance HTML has one DOM-free typed presentation owner over Conversation Sync block fields; retained runtime supplies only lexical compatibility names and owns no provenance rendering policy.

Assistant serving-route presentation has one pure typed owner over the canonical last response-authoring round; internal compaction and billed-but-discarded calls never become the displayed response model or provider.
Write-gate refusal normalization and user-facing HTML have one DOM-free typed presentation owner; structured and legacy facts converge before retained write cards receive badge and notice strings.

Tool-catalog, web/fetch, vertical-domain, and engine-breakdown presentation has one DOM-free typed owner; retained dispatch receives an immutable port while explicit scan and display budgets bound every result family.

Image reading, inspection, generation, and editing presentation has one DOM-free typed owner; retained dispatch receives one immutable port while explicit URL policy and scan/display budgets bound every image family.

Browser JavaScript execution presentation has one DOM-free typed owner; retained dispatch receives one immutable port while pre-parse, code, description, and result display budgets are explicit and every truncation is visible.

Command execution presentation has one DOM-free typed owner; retained code owns timer, interrupt I/O, and interaction lifecycles only, while explicit parse, text, legacy-tail, and QR budgets bound every rendered command card.

Pending write-tool approval presentation has one DOM-free typed owner; risk metadata projection is explicitly bounded, approval ids remain escaped data rather than executable action text, and retained code owns dispatch order only.

Synthetic context-injection presentation has one DOM-free typed owner; swarm, peer, operator-steer, and stall-nudge lanes have a closed priority order, explicit item/text/XML budgets, and injected Markdown, icon, title, and translation ports while retained code owns chronology and jump lifecycle only.

Human Guidance presentation has one DOM-free typed owner; awaiting, expired, skipped, and submitted states share a closed order, question/option/id budgets are explicit, and untrusted response values remain escaped datasets consumed by static delegated actions.

Human Guidance delegated responses have one lifecycle-scoped typed UI owner; card-scoped static selectors require agreeing bounded datasets, responses are capped before translation and transport, submissions are single-flight per conversation and guidance identity, optimistic state rolls back exactly, and expired versus transport failures remain distinct. Retained code owns EN-to-CN arrival translation only and consumes the presentation store through a lexical port rather than a runtime global.
Fetch-like response projection and canonical result-error recovery have one typed owner; retained consumers receive its immutable port only as a static lexical dependency.
Bounded asynchronous fan-out has one typed owner; conversation recovery sweeps share an explicit four-worker budget and isolate per-item failures.

Page and network wake recovery has one lifecycle-owned typed application controller; it selects only conversations with live attempts, shares the bounded work pool, and removes every listener on teardown.

Backend process liveness and Sidecar storage readiness have separate typed verdict owners over shared stateless ports; push/browser signals only trigger the two-probe liveness arbiter, while storage recovery polling is visibility-aware, single-flight, and disposable.

Application dialogs have one lazy typed page-lifecycle service and one DOM controller; at most one overlay is active, replacement and destroy settle safe defaults, and every keyboard listener, animation frame, interval, and exit timer is disposable.
Swarm push telemetry has one typed subscription and transient-Turn presentation owner; start/destroy is idempotent and durable Turn projection remains untouched until authoritative hydration.

Browser startup coordinates metadata catalogs and active presentation through one typed application owner whose port surface cannot hydrate or dispatch a Turn; folder failure and retry remain independent from conversation catalog loading.

Authoritative conversation catalog loading has one typed application owner; server rows apply before reconstructible cache writes, cache work retains one in-flight and one latest pending page, and a 304 without its complete in-memory snapshot forces one unconditional recovery request.
Explicit single-conversation refresh is one injected application command over the authoritative Turn runtime; it owns no catalog, transport, retry, or browser-global state.

Local catalog metadata reconciliation has one typed application owner; busy conversations keep authoritative activity timestamps, cross-tab invalidation remains a wake hint, and sidebar scheduling permits at most one pending frame.

Send preparation is one conversation-keyed typed transient-Turn controller; switching views cannot redirect teardown to the wrong conversation, and scroll presentation cannot invalidate its state transition.
Cookie-capture completion subscription and toast projection have one lifecycle-scoped typed controller; composition waits for retained push initialization and publishes no browser global.

My Context preference resolution and undo presentation have one typed controller over injected mutation, translation, icon, and failure ports; runtime action names are dispatch entries, not browser globals.
Shared fullscreen-image and generated-image download actions have one typed DOM owner with an explicit overlay, keyboard-listener, and temporary-anchor lifecycle.
The browser chat-model capability taxonomy is one typed server-projected controller; retained pickers may fail open but never recreate its exclusion policy.
Browser model grouping is one typed policy with an injected brand detector; retained pickers never infer a second vendor grouping or publish the policy on window.
Model brand detection, brand badge assets, display-name ordering, and role-avatar assets have separate DOM-free typed owners; retained helper names exist only as composition aliases.
Backend-authored model fold metadata has one pure typed display projection; recent-model persistence is a separate injected controller bounded to five IDs.

Browser ZIP package upload has one typed lazy transport owner shared by Memory and Skills; it accepts ZIP files only, permits one active upload, and installs one fixed page-lifetime listener set per surface.

My Day TODO and stream writes have one typed lazy controller over explicit API, selected-report, cache, render, and diagnostic ports; optimistic changes roll back on rejection and server responses own resolved status and reports.
My Day quick actions have one typed lazy intent controller; the composer is prefilled before conversation creation, and tool modes cross explicit presentation ports.
Retained runtime debt may only shrink until its target is zero.

legacyDebt.remedy: Move an owner into frontend/src/conversation or another typed feature and remove its manifest entry.
Delete retained JavaScript as typed owners replace it; do not move debt between sections.
Compose the bounded Human Guidance presentation store as a lexical port; do not publish mutable response presentation state through runtimeScope.
Delegate restricted response entries to the typed Human Guidance action controller; project.js must not regain DOM, translation, transport, rollback, or presentation authority.
Use the typed owner-scoped conversation metadata cache; retained code may consume only its lexical compatibility port.
Compose the typed backend- and storage-availability owners; do not recreate a retained verdict, timer, banner, action, or browser global.
Compose the typed application-dialog controller; retained consumers may use lexical aliases but may not own dialog DOM, timers, or global services.
Use the owner-scoped typed report repository and disposable idle-background lifecycle.
Dispatch a turn command or event and derive the document from TurnStore.
Read ordered Turns through ConversationTurnRead; conversation shells are metadata only.
Capture composer settings once and persist them through persistConversationSettings, independent of Turn content.
Consume backend-authored Turn lifecycle and settlement; do not infer or stamp a parallel frontend reconciliation verdict.
Use ConversationSurface and stable Turn/block identity; do not recreate a parallel DOM owner.
Name catalog metadata by its Turn meaning: _turnSnapshotRequired, _serverTurnCount, and _catalogTurnCount.
Let ConversationSurface reconcile the affected turn by stable identity.
Dispatch a UI intent or store action; ConversationSurface owns the DOM application.
Resolve and reconcile nodes by turnId or blockId, never by array position.
Render running and terminal revisions into the same turnId-keyed node.
Read live attempt state from the conversation session store.
Use projectionRevision and stable block revisions instead of content heuristics.
Retire the projected messages document after all block renderers and action intents use TurnStore directly.
Replace retained renderMessage parity one content block at a time, then delete the compatibility port and adapter.
Keep scroll and loading presentation in the lifecycle-scoped ConversationSurface host, never on the conversation shell.
Inject the scroll viewport only; ConversationSurface owns capture, restore, follow suspension, and disposal.
Observe ConversationTurnRead and the active Surface; diagnostics must not fetch or parse a second transcript document.
Backfill stable segment blocks for archived turns and remove content/thinking/toolRounds fallback projection.
